introduction_markdown: This paper is arranged in two sections, A and B. Answer ALL questions in Sections A and B. Section A: answer ALL the questions (15 questions); the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: answer ALL four questions; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.
enonce_intro_markdown:
![fig-1](gce-ol-maths-2021-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_11_fig_1.png)

Figure 2 is a circle with centre $O$ and $SR$ is a tangent. Given that angle $OPQ = 24^\circ$.

Find the value of:

figures.legende: Figure 2: circle with centre O, diameter PS, chords PQ, PT, QT, QS, TS, OQ; SR is a tangent at S; P, Q, R on one line; angles x (at O), y (at T) and m (at R) to find.

incertitudes: Figure 2 (Q11) : le sujet imprime « SR is a tangent » seulement ; d'après le dessin, P, Q et R sont alignés (la droite PQ prolongée passe par R) et x désigne l'angle POQ (la lettre x est écrite entre OP et OQ), y l'angle PTQ (entre TP et TQ) et m l'angle PRS. Réponses 132, 66 et 66 selon cette lecture ; si x était l'angle QOS, ce serait 48.

questions.corrige_markdown:
$x$ is the angle $POQ$ at the centre. $OP=OQ$ (radii), so triangle $OPQ$ is isosceles and $\angle OQP = \angle OPQ = 24^\circ$.

Angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$: $x = 180^\circ - 24^\circ - 24^\circ = 132^\circ$.

**$x = 132^\circ$.**

$PS$ is a diameter (it passes through the centre $O$), so the angle in a semicircle gives $\angle PQS = 90^\circ$.

In triangle $PQS$: $\angle PSQ = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 24^\circ = 66^\circ$.

$y = \angle PTQ$ and $\angle PSQ$ are angles in the same segment, standing on the same chord $PQ$, so they are equal.

**$y = 66^\circ$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Angle $m$. *[6 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$SR$ is a tangent and $OS$ is a radius, so $\angle PSR = 90^\circ$ (tangent perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact).

The points $P$, $Q$, $R$ are in a straight line, so in triangle $PSR$: $\angle SPR = 24^\circ$ and $\angle PSR = 90^\circ$.

$m = \angle PRS = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 24^\circ = 66^\circ$.

(Check with the alternate segment theorem: $\angle QSR = \angle QPS = 24^\circ$; in triangle $QSR$, $\angle SQR = 90^\circ$, so $m = 180^\circ-90^\circ-24^\circ=66^\circ$.)

**$m = 66^\circ$.**
